```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This is the fastest way to see real popgenVCF output: no Docker, no download,
no configuration file. The package ships a small but real dataset -- 160
individuals from 8 populations in the 1000 Genomes Project's chromosome 22,
X, and Y callsets -- and every analysis runs on it exactly as it would on
your own VCF.

Prefer to look before running anything? [Results and Interpretation](https://github.com/duceppemo/popgenVCF/wiki/Results-and-Interpretation)
shows real figures from this exact dataset, and the complete
[example PDF report](https://github.com/duceppemo/popgenVCF/blob/main/docs/examples/chr22-quickstart-report.pdf)
is committed in the repository.

## 1. Locate the bundled dataset

```r
library(popgenVCF)
paths <- quickstart_dataset_paths()
paths
```

See `system.file("extdata", "quickstart", "README.md", package = "popgenVCF")`
for exactly which real samples and populations are included and why (it
deliberately contains a known real duplicate/MZ-twin pair, so the kinship
analysis below has genuine, verifiable signal -- and, as a bonus, a
cautionary real example of why a single flagged pair needs corroborating
evidence, not blind acceptance; see "What to look for" below).

## 2. Run the pipeline

```r
cfg <- default_config()
cfg$input$vcf <- paths$vcf
cfg$input$metadata <- paths$metadata
cfg$output$directory <- tempfile("popgenvcf-quickstart-")
cfg$compute$threads <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)

analysis <- run_pipeline(cfg)
```

On a modern multi-core machine this takes a few minutes -- most of the time
is DAPC's cross-validation across the default `K = 2:10` range, run in full
because it is exactly what a real analysis does. Every module runs with its
documented defaults: QC and LD pruning, PCA, IBS, kinship, sex check, runs
of homozygosity, FST (and its Nm gene-flow estimate), genome scans, linkage
disequilibrium decay, LD-based effective population size, population
genetic distance and tree, a population assignment test, diversity
(including allelic richness), DAPC, AMOVA, and a neighbour-joining tree of
individuals.
Mantel/isolation-by-distance runs too: the bundled metadata includes real,
documented population-level collection-site coordinates (see the dataset's
`README.md` for the exact source and caveats), so the analysis has real
geographic distances to work with rather than being skipped.

## 3. Look at the output

```r
list.files(cfg$output$directory)
browseURL(file.path(cfg$output$directory, "report", "population_genomics_report.html"))
```

`report/population_genomics_report.pdf` is the compact, portable
counterpart. Both are self-contained -- copy either one without the rest of
the result directory. `tables/` and `figures/` hold every individual result;
`analysis_results.rds` is the complete serialized object for further work in
R (`get_analysis_result(analysis, "kinship")`, and so on).

## 4. What to look for

- **Kinship** (`tables/36_close_relatives.tsv`, `figures/21_kinship_heatmap`):
  both seeded high-kinship pairs show up classified `duplicate/MZ twin` with
  kinship near 0.5, but only one of them actually is a duplicate.
  `NA19331`/`NA19334` (both LWK) are confirmed consistent: real, matching
  male chromosome X and Y genotypes, no contradicting evidence.
  `HG03873`/`HG03998` (labelled as two *different* populations, ITU and STU)
  is the more interesting case: sex check below shows their real chromosome
  X and Y genotypes are genuinely different sexes, which rules out MZ
  twins/duplicate despite the high autosomal kinship -- a real example of
  why a single flagged pair needs corroborating evidence, not blind
  acceptance.
- **Sex check** (`tables/42_sex_check.tsv`, `figures/27_sex_check_F_by_sample`):
  genetic sex inferred from chromosome X heterozygosity *and* chromosome Y
  call rate together, compared against the bundled `sex` metadata column.
  When the two signals confidently disagree the combined call is
  `discordant`, not silently resolved -- this is what actually reveals the
  `HG03873`/`HG03998` kinship caveat above.
- **PCA** (`figures/07_PCA_PC1_PC2`): the 8 populations should separate
  broadly by continental origin. `figures/07b_PCA_PC1_PC2_by_sex` is the
  same PCA fit recoloured by the bundled `sex` metadata column instead --
  one static panel per metadata column that qualifies (enough samples per
  value; see the [interpretation guide](interpreting-results.html) for the
  exact rule). Sex should show no separation here, which is itself the
  expected, useful result: population structure, not sex, drives this PCA.
- **Runs of homozygosity** (`tables/38_ROH_sample_summary.tsv`): `FROH` is
  scaled to this run's ~1Mb analyzed footprint, not the whole genome -- see
  the [interpretation guide](interpreting-results.html) before comparing it
  to anything else.
- **Mantel/isolation by distance** (`tables/25_Mantel_IBD_summary.tsv`,
  `figures/12_isolation_by_distance`): a real, statistically significant
  positive signal (Mantel r = 0.313, p = 0.001) -- genetic distance increases
  with geographic distance across these 8 continentally diverse populations.
  A partial Mantel test controlling for population identity (r = 0.163,
  p = 0.001) shows the signal weakens but survives once population
  membership is accounted for -- see the
  [interpretation guide](interpreting-results.html) for what this means.
- **LD-based effective population size** (`tables/45_Ne_LD.tsv`): needs
  markers on at least two chromosomes to work at all, and this dataset's
  retained autosomal marker set is chr22-only by design, so every population
  correctly reports an honest "insufficient data" skip here -- see the
  [interpretation guide](interpreting-results.html) for what a real
  multi-chromosome VCF produces instead.
- **Population genetic distance and tree** (`tables/46_population_genetic_distance.tsv`,
  `trees/population_Nei_neighbor_joining.nwk`): Nei's standard genetic
  distance between populations, unlike the sample-level kinship/tree
  results above. `LWK`/`YRI` (both African) are the closest pair; the
  largest distances are all African-vs-non-African pairs -- real
  continental population structure.
- **Population assignment test** (`tables/47_population_assignment.tsv`,
  `figures/47_population_assignment`): 66% of samples correctly self-assign
  to their recorded population from genotype alone; most of the rest are
  `ITU`/`STU` or `LWK`/`YRI` cross-assignments -- exactly the same two
  closely related population pairs the FST/Nm and Nei's-distance results
  above already flagged, a real cross-method confirmation rather than a
  method weakness.

## 5. Next steps

Once the shape of the output is familiar, move to your own data with the
[Getting Started](https://github.com/duceppemo/popgenVCF/wiki/Getting-Started)
guide, which covers Docker/Apptainer execution, metadata preparation, and
configuration in full.
